title: mfbdfm: A Mixed-Frequency Bayesian Dynamic Factor Model
text: mfbdfm estimates Bayesian mixed-frequency dynamic factor model: single dynamic factor extracted indicators observed different frequencies, optionally anchored target series factor directly interpretable series’ growth rate rather generic activity index. package ships flagship application, Weekly Activity Index (WAI), high-frequency GDP indicator Switzerland anchored GDP growth, vignette uses worked example throughout. WAI built combine two kinds data: Conventional macroeconomic indicators — surveys, prices, trade, purchasing manager indices — published monthly quarterly, Alternative high-frequency data — payment transaction volumes, mobility indicators, search-trend indices, traffic flight counts — available daily weekly, often short histories irregular publication lags. Unlike unsupervised approaches extract factor high-frequency data alone (e.g. principal components), WAI supervised: identification restriction anchors factor observed GDP growth, direct high-frequency proxy GDP rather generic activity index merely correlates . methodology, full empirical results, real-time forecast evaluation described Kronenberg (2026); see ?mfbdfm full citation underlying multi-factor framework Eckert, Kronenberg, Mikosch & Neuwirth (2025). vignette covers package’s user-facing workflow .

title: mfbdfm: A Mixed-Frequency Bayesian Dynamic Factor Model
text: ind_dfm() estimates single latent weekly factor ftf_t whose (distributed-lag, temporally aggregated) measurement equation links every input series, whose autoregressive state equation includes stochastic volatility variance common shocks can rise crises instead smoothed away. Three features make work real-world mixed-frequency data: Data augmentation treats missing lower-frequency observations latent states, series starts 2020 updates weekly, another starts 1990 updates monthly, quarterly GDP can enter state-space model. Stochastic volatility factor state equation lets abrupt swings (e.g. COVID-19 pandemic) show genuinely higher volatility rather averaged away. Quasi-differencing measurement equation removes serial correlation series’ idiosyncratic errors, persistent indicator-specific noise doesn’t get misattributed common factor. Identification fixes factor’s loading target series (GDP) one shrinks measurement error toward zero, factor tracks GDP growth closely construction — see ?ind_dfm details references, vignette("mfbdfm")’s “Real-time GDP vintages” section target series constructed live use.

title: mfbdfm: A Mixed-Frequency Bayesian Dynamic Factor Model — mfbdfm-package
text: model extracts single dynamic factor, constrained identification restriction fixes loading GDP one, factor directly interpretable weekly GDP growth rather generic activity index. Three features let combine heterogeneous, incomplete high-frequency data official GDP figures: Data augmentation treats missing mixed-frequency observations latent states, series can enter different starting dates, publication lags frequencies (weekly, monthly, quarterly). Stochastic volatility factor state equation lets variance common shocks vary time, crisis-period swings (e.g. COVID-19 pandemic) mechanically smoothed away. Quasi-differencing (Chib & Greenberg, 1994) removes serial correlation measurement errors, preventing persistent idiosyncratic noise individual indicators contaminating common factor. Estimation Gibbs sampling using precision sampler Chan Jeliazkov (2009), temporal aggregation flow variables following geometric-mean approximation Mariano Murasawa (2003).
